teams.heading: Jake White dreams of Fiji hosting Ireland in Suva one day
teams.body: White, speaking before the match, said there would be nothing greater than Fiji hosting Ireland in Suva, and he plans to move to Fiji in early 2027 to coach schools and clubs as well as the national side. The Aviva result went Ireland's way: Fiji lost 15-43, with a 26-0 second-half response settling a contest that was only 17-15 at the break. He credits timing for landing the job: "I believe everything in life is timing."

lead.why: It is the only NEW Fiji-focused item on the shortlist, and it gives a fan something new about White's plans beyond the Dublin result.

teams.heading: Max Ojomoh shines at inside centre as England rout Japan 78-15
teams.body: Planet Rugby's takeaways from Saturday's 78-15 win over Japan single out Max Ojomoh, who starred at inside centre, and the first minute backs them up: he threw the miss-pass that sent Will Joseph away for the opener. Japan were a man short from the start, Harry Hockings having been sent off for a dangerous hit on Ellis Genge, and England were 42 points clear by the half-hour. Henry Pollock, who had fancied the 14 shirt, is rumoured to be fuming, with Joseph wearing it after Immanuel Feyi-Waboso's injury ended his tournament.

lead.why: A named England player and a fresh tactical angle on Saturday's win, separate from the Joseph record story already run today.

teams.heading: Antoine Dupont hailed by press after France's 21-19 win over South Africa
teams.body: Friday's 21-19 win over South Africa at the Stade de France is still generating praise for Antoine Dupont, who wore the No. 10 shirt. Planete Rugby's review, quoted in Midi Olympique's international press round-up, says he was decisive in two of the three tries and ran the game with magisterial control. Midi Olympique's James While called it one of the greatest individual performances he has covered in a test match. The review argues Dupont has largely undermined the arguments raised against him.

lead.why: A post-match reaction to France's win over South Africa, centred on Antoine Dupont, is a fresh France story that is not the already-reported Marchand news.

teams.heading: Tommy O'Brien and Baloucoune score braces as Ireland beat Fiji 43-15
teams.body: Ireland are four wins from five in the Nations Championship, but ESPN's report judged the performance flattered to deceive despite the braces. Fiji had been heavily beaten by France in Lyon the week before, and new coach Jake White, who took the job last month, was still bedding in his side. Farrell's men now turn to South Africa, which The42 casts as Ireland's true final of the window, after a 42-12 win over Argentina the previous weekend.

lead.why: A fresh post-match report on the Fiji result, naming the two try scorers, and the first new item on the shortlist.

teams.heading: Argentina coach Contepomi says Italy dominated first half but failed to finish
teams.body: Argentina coach Felipe Contepomi, speaking after the 19-14 win in Genoa, conceded that Italy had controlled possession and territory in the first half. His point was that in matches like this, the side that converts pressure into points wins, and Italy's problem was finishing. Captain Pablo Matera joined him at the press conference. Contepomi also said the Pumas kept their composure after playing a stretch with 13 men, calling his squad a team still under construction. Argentina next face France in Paris.

lead.why: It is the only new item with an Italy-specific angle; #1 and #3 repeat the already-reported result, #4 is about Argentina, and #5 is U20 news about a match already played.

teams.heading: Tuipulotu admits Scotland let themselves down in New Zealand defeat
teams.body: Scotland captain Sione Tuipulotu, born and raised in Melbourne, says the squad have confronted their 21-43 defeat by New Zealand. "It is always hard to watch the footage back after a defeat like that where we missed some big opportunities and let ourselves down in certain areas," he said. Tuipulotu expects Australia to arrive wounded after their 45-22 defeat by England at Twickenham, and says he will always carry extra fire against the Wallabies.

lead.why: Scotland's captain speaking before the match is a fresh, Scotland-centred angle, and the Joey Sharp item has already run today.

teams.heading: Wales stun All Blacks 35-28 in Cardiff, first win since 1953
teams.body: Wales held firm through the final 25 minutes at the Principality Stadium on Saturday, after Peter Lakai's try had cut the lead to seven points. New Zealand were repeatedly held up over the Welsh line as the hosts ground out the finish, ending a 34-match losing run against the three-time Rugby World Cup winners. Tomos Williams had a hand in every Welsh try, scoring one himself, and Steve Tandy's side made five changes from the win over Japan.

lead.why: It is the newest item and the result itself, and a fan would text a mate about the first win over the All Blacks since 1953.

teams.heading: Felipe Contepomi credits Pumas' character after grinding out 19-14 win in Genoa
teams.body: Felipe Contepomi said the 19-14 win over Italy in Genoa owed more to character than control. Italy had dominated possession and territory in the first half, the Argentina coach acknowledged, and the final 20 minutes were very complicated as the Pumas finished with 13 men after yellow cards. Contepomi said the squad had stayed connected and found a way to win, and that Argentina have a good base to build on. He described a team still under construction, with two weeks together ahead of the trip to France.

lead.why: Contepomi's post-match press conference is the fresh same-team reaction to Saturday's win, and it is not yet in the edition's coverage.

teams.heading: Harry Wilson hunts ruthless Wallabies response to Scotland, citing Springboks win
teams.body: Wallabies captain Harry Wilson says the side has taken inspiration from their win over the Springboks in Perth as they seek a response to a three-game losing streak. Wilson recalled Australia blowing South Africa away in the first hour before holding on through several late cards. He wants that edge back: "Just the ruthless mindset we had there and that's what we want to see more of this weekend." Carter Gordon's return at flyhalf adds to the attacking case.

lead.why: A new captain's-eve comment from Harry Wilson on how the Springboks win shapes the Wallabies' response, and it is about Australia's own stake in the test.

teams.heading: Warner Dearns and Opeti Helu score as Japan lose 78-15 at Twickenham
teams.body: England ran in 13 tries in a 78-15 win, leading 32-3 inside 20 minutes. Will Joseph, back after four years out of the Test game, scored five of them, a record-equalling haul, with Max Ojomoh's midfield running setting up two. Japan's tries came through co-captain Warner Dearns and Opeti Helu, but they could not match England's ball movement or the quick rucks that have troubled bigger sides. Their next assignment is in Scotland.

lead.why: A fresh match report on Japan's Saturday defeat, with Japan's own try-scorers and a clear decisive moment in the 32-3 lead.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie admits All Blacks were 'one-dimensional' in 35-28 Wales defeat
teams.body: Rennie admitted the All Blacks 'got a bit one-dimensional' as Wales won 35-28 in Cardiff, their first win over New Zealand since 1953. He pointed to the errors rather than the scoreboard: nine turnovers in the first half, four of them from offloads, and three attempts held up over the line in the second. Rennie said the review would cover selection and substitutions as well as the team's decision-making, and that the squad expects more of itself.

lead.why: A fresh post-match reaction from the head coach on the Wales defeat, the strongest new New Zealand story in today's pack.

teams.heading: Ruan Nortjé rejects card excuse after Springboks' 21-19 defeat in Paris
teams.body: Ruan Nortjé would not use Jasper Wiese's 20-minute red card or Lood de Jager's yellow as an excuse after Friday's Stade de France defeat, pointing out that France were a man down for 30 minutes too. "We can't put the blame on that at all," the lock said, before conceding the defeat leaves South Africa relying on other results for the Nations Championship final, with Ireland next. "It's going to be all about looking at what we did wrong and what we can improve," Nortjé said.

lead.why: It is a new same-team post-match reaction from a Springbok, and it sets up what South Africa need next.
